articles.title: PHP2Shell flaws attract millions of reported exploit attempts after patches
articles.dek: Cloudflare sees a surge in hostile requests, which must not be confused with confirmed breaches.
articles.summary: Security providers reported intense exploitation traffic after two PHP vulnerabilities were disclosed on 21 October. Cloudflare said it observed millions of potentially malicious requests across its network.
body: Amazon Threat Intelligence reported exploit attempts hitting its defensive sensors as early as 17 October, before public disclosure. Activity before an embargo ends highlights the limits of coordinated vulnerability disclosure.
PHP maintainers issued emergency fixes and urged updates. Website operators must verify installed versions, exposure and successful application of security patches.
Millions of attempts do not establish millions of compromised systems. The true extent and outcome of exploitation remain uncertain.

questions.answer: Security monitoring detected many suspicious requests after two flaws were disclosed; attempts are not equivalent to millions of successful intrusions.

questions.answer: Each service operator needs to check installed versions and available patches; publishing a fix does not automatically update every server.

articles.title: GitLab releases fixes for critical CVSS-10 remote execution flaw
articles.dek: Under specific conditions the flaw could enable unauthenticated code execution.
articles.summary: GitLab released patched Community and Enterprise editions on 21 October. On 22 October, Singapore's cybersecurity authority and Italy's CERT-GARR warned about CVE-2026-110264, rated 10.0 out of 10 on the CVSS scale.
body: The issue involves an integer overflow when compiling a crafted regular expression. In certain conditions a remote unauthenticated attacker could execute code on a vulnerable server, potentially exposing code repositories and development workflows.
GitLab advised operators to install compatible updates including 19.5.1, 19.4.3, 19.3.6 and backports. The vendor said its managed instances were patched.
The maximum technical severity rating is not a measure of how many systems were actually breached. No comprehensive confirmed compromise count was established.
Sources distinguish what was reported on 22 October from scenarios and consequences not yet established. Security or financing announcements should not be described as fully realized effects.

articles.title: Capcom reports unauthorized access to 11.77 million customer records
articles.dek: The company confirms exposed emails and account metadata, with 196 passwords changed by an intruder.
articles.summary: On 22 October Capcom reported an intrusion affecting 11,774,247 CAPCOM ID records containing email addresses, account activity information and last-login IP addresses.
body: A subset of 43 records included other personal fields such as date of birth and country. The company identified unauthorized password changes on 196 accounts and reset them.
Capcom said credit-card information was not involved and original login passwords were not confirmed stolen. It advised users to watch for phishing messages impersonating the company.
The number refers to affected records, not 11.77 million confirmed stolen passwords, or a count of unique victims. Investigation continued.
Sources distinguish what was reported on 22 October from scenarios and consequences not yet established. Security or financing announcements should not be described as fully realized effects.

questions.question: How many CAPCOM ID accounts were affected by the reported access?
questions.answer: Capcom reported unauthorized access involving records associated with about 11.77 million accounts, with some additional personal details for a subset of 43.

questions.question: Does the account count show that passwords or payment details were stolen?
questions.answer: No. The number of affected records is distinct from the types of data exposed; the company did not confirm theft of all original passwords or banking information.

articles.title: Meta proposes non-voting Class C shares to help finance AI investment
articles.dek: The new share class is scheduled for January 2027 and would preserve Zuckerberg's voting control.
articles.summary: Meta announced on 21 October a plan, scrutinized by markets on the 22nd, to establish listed non-voting Class C shares for potential financing, employee awards and acquisitions supporting its artificial intelligence expansion.
body: Company filings say the additional capital-raising option could help fund large infrastructure projects without reducing Mark Zuckerberg's voting power. Creating a class of shares is not equivalent to selling shares and receiving the funds immediately.
Management expects eventual returns from models and data centres. Investors are weighing spending levels and economic dilution to existing shareholders even if the voting structure remains unchanged.
The proposed effective date is January 2027; as of 22 October it had not raised all the funds envisioned. Future revenue projections remain uncertain.

articles.title: Anthropic explores a possible November IPO as AI markets turn cautious
articles.dek: Reuters and Bloomberg report preparatory plans, but the offering dates remain uncertain.
articles.summary: On 22 October Reuters reported that Anthropic was proceeding with preparations for a possible mid-November initial public offering. Bloomberg had already described a similar tentative timetable in early October; people briefed on plans warned that timing could change.
body: An IPO could give outside investors shares and provide capital to the company. It does not mean the company has already completed a listing, raised funds or obtained a fixed market valuation.

Several AI infrastructure operators delayed offerings amid higher borrowing costs and volatile markets. Supporters argue investors still want exposure to leading AI models, despite doubts about capital intensity.
The potential valuation of up to $1.5 trillion was a reported estimate, not a finalized share price. Prospectus and marketing dates remained provisional.
